messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple container restarts observed on path /v1/generate (model: redwood-extend-65b) across gpu-node-07. Error snippet: "CUDA out of memory during prefill step". 10+ restarts in last 3m. Paging on-call.

pagerduty: Paging matt_oc (primary on-call) — please acknowledge. Escalation policy: 4m.

matt_oc: acked. jumping in. can someone drop the most recent stack/logs?

ana_sre: attaching latest kube logs (snip):
```
2025-11-02T18:12:30Z runtime: prefill failed: cudaMemcpyAsync: out of memory
container_restart_count=3 pod/gpu-node-07-runtime-xyz
oom-killer: process killed
```

chris_runtime: confirm it's prefill OOM not during decode. We're seeing KV cache allocation spike if prompt length > 250k tokens (customer long prompt). That blows memory during prefill when we allocate key/values.

june_support: We're seeing several customer error spikes — 502/503s on /v1/generate. I pulled a couple request IDs: req_9f3a, req_d1b2. Customers flagged: acme-infra (non-prod), healthcare-beta (prod). Both report failed requests ~18:11-18:15 UTC.

yuki_ml: model variant huggingface/redwood-extend-65b-int8 is in use for these requests. That variant still allocates KV in full float32 before quantization in prefill path. Might be a regression after last deploy.

matt_oc: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) throttle or block very long-context requests at gateway, 2) route traffic off gpu-node-07, 3) switch this model to quantized runtime that pre-allocates smaller KV, 4) restart pod with eviction protection off? prefer non-disruptive first.

chris_runtime: agree. Doing a quick routing change: adding a temporary rule to divert new /v1/generate traffic for redwood-extend-65b away from gpu-node-07. executing now.

console-bot: Route update applied: traffic split for model redwood-extend-65b -> {gpu-pool: 0%, dedicated-pool: 100%} (change id: rsplit-20251102-1).

matt_oc: nice. but those in-flight heavy prefill requests will still hit pods and might restart. we should also set a soft prompt-length cap at the proxy level to stop extremely long prefill sizes while we investigate. can we push a temporary rule?

ana_sre: pushing rate-limit rule now: 
```
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.dev/api/rate-limits \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"path":"/v1/generate","model":"redwood-extend-65b","max_tokens_in_request":100000}'
```
Applied. :white_check_mark: This will reject >100k token prefill requests with 400 immediately.

june_support: I posted to affected customers that we're throttling extremely long prompts temporarily to reduce errors — asked them to resend trimmed prompts. ticket# INC-2025-311.

yuki_ml: quick check: we should also consider forcing the runtime to allocate KV in int8/quantized path during prefill. chris, do we have a hotfix for quantized prefill?

chris_runtime: we have a branch that defers float32 expansion until after quantized checksum. I can promote a canary build to the non-prod pool in 10m. But for prod I want more testing. For now the routing + proxy cap reduces blast radius.

matt_oc: good. also get kube to cordon gpu-node-07 so new pods don't land there. we suspect a bad hardware/driver state might exacerbate OOMs. ana can you cordon and drain gracefully?

ana_sre: cordoning gpu-node-07 now. draining pods with graceful 60s. `kubectl cordon gpu-node-07` then `kubectl drain gpu-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: node cordoned. draining started. 5 pods evicted.

chris_runtime: while draining, I'm rolling a config change to enable prefill guardrails on runtime: set ENV PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=120000 for model redwood-extend-65b. Will roll to dedicated-pool first.

console-bot: Rolling config to dedicated-pool: rollout id cfg-roll-20251102-2. Expected completion 3m.

yuki_ml: note for postmortem: we should track token accounting differences between gateway and runtime. Some SDKs send raw characters; gateway tokenization mismatch allowed too-large logical token count to reach runtime. save that for RCA.

june_support: monitoring shows 503 error rate dropped from 12% to 1.5% after route change + rate cap. customers pinged. acme-infra back to normal, healthcare-beta partially recovered (some retries required).

matt_oc: good. next: prepare incident summary for on-call handoff. chris — can you try to reproduce locally with a 300k token prompt to confirm prefill OOM pattern? also capture heap/KV footprints.

chris_runtime: started a repro on a staging gpu with a synthetic 300k token request. Confirmed: prefill spikes GPU alloc to near full, then CUDA OOM in allocator during memcpy. Logs: `RuntimeAllocator::alloc failed: cuMemAlloc failed (out of memory)`. Will capture memory profile and share.

ana_sre: also checking node GPU driver logs — no driver hangs, just typical allocation failures. suspect workload pattern rather than hardware.

matt_oc: ok. next steps timeline: immediate mitigations (done): traffic routing, rate cap, node cordon/drain. Short-term: runtime config guardrail and canary quantized path. Mid-term: implement gateway token-count verification + reject at edge, and add per-model prefill memory accounting and admission control. Long-term: change prefill to stream KV allocation + fallback to CPU for oversized prefill.

june_support: I've drafted a customer-facing postmortem stub and notified the CS leads. Will escalate high-sev customers if they request.

yuki_ml: I'll open a model onboarding ticket to improve quantized prefill behavior and add tests for >200k prompts.

incident-bot: Handoff reminder — matt_oc handing off to next on-call ana_sre in 1h. Please add notes to #incidents-runbook.

matt_oc: I'm going offline in 55m. ana, any concerns to pick up?

ana_sre: I'll monitor the node drain, rollout, and error rates. If error rate rises above 3% we'll rollback routing change and escalate. I've set a CloudWatch/console alert.

chris_runtime: posted memory profile and repro steps to the thread and created PR for canary quantized runtime (PR #8421). reviewers: @yuki_ml @matt_oc.

june_support: updated ticket INC-2025-311 with mitigation timeline and customer notifications. closing immediate incident Slack thread but will ping here on updates. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Closed? false.

matt_oc: thanks all. good run. will file full postmortem tomorrow with timeline, root cause hypothesis, and action items.

ana_sre: acknowledged handoff. continuing monitoring.

(End of thread)
